title: What is 5642 times 2, and is Everest twice as tall as Elbrus?
description: The height of Elbrus is doubled by splitting it into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones, and the result is compared with the height of Everest. Keeko doubts this and says Everest really is twice as tall because the picture shows it.
teaching_notes: One idea: to multiply a large number by 2, double each part and add the parts, then compare with the other height. Watch for students who trust the look of a picture over the product.

video_script.why: The child doubles the height of Elbrus exactly and compares it with the height of Everest to test the claim of the picture.
video_script.substitution: The height of Elbrus of the book is doubled by splitting it into parts.
video_script.anchor: the lifelike mountain range of the book, where Everest appears to be twice as tall as Elbrus, with the heights of the two mountains
video_script.wrong_answer: everest really is twice as tall
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko trusts the picture and says Everest really is twice as tall as Elbrus. Twice Elbrus is 11284 m, which is more than 8848 m, the height of Everest, so the claim is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Everest is not twice as tall as Elbrus, because twice Elbrus is more than Everest

final_answer.value: 11284, which is more than 8848, so Everest is not twice as tall as Elbrus.
final_answer.spoken: eleven thousand two hundred and eighty four, which is more than eight thousand eight hundred and forty eight, so Everest is not twice as tall as Elbrus

maths_rules: Elbrus is 5642 m and Everest is 8848 m
8848 is less than 11284, so Everest is not twice as tall as Elbrus
video_script.design: The height of Elbrus is split into place values and each part is doubled. The sum is set beside the height of Everest on a bar, and Everest falls short.

<bookmark mark='range'/>Everest looks twice as tall as Elbrus. Elbrus is five thousand six hundred and forty two metres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What do we get when we double the height of Elbrus?

narration: <bookmark mark='bar'/>Twice a height means two copies of it, one on top of the other.
<bookmark mark='copy'/>We can find it by doubling each place of the number.

beats.on_screen: Given: Elbrus 5642 m; Everest 8848 m; Everest appears twice as tall as Elbrus

marks.given: the two heights and the claim are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, Elbrus is five thousand six hundred and forty two metres. Everest is eight thousand eight hundred and forty eight metres.

beats.on_screen: To find: 5642 x 2, and whether Everest is twice as tall as Elbrus
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find twice the height of Elbrus, and compare it with Everest.

marks.split: the number splits into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, split the height into five thousand, six hundred, forty and two.

marks.thousands: two times five thousand is written
marks.hundreds: two times six hundred is written
marks.rest: two times forty and two times two are written

narration: <bookmark mark='thousands'/>Step two, double each part. Two times five thousand is ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='hundreds'/>Two times six hundred is one thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Two times forty is eighty, and two times two is four.

marks.first: ten thousand and one thousand two hundred are added
marks.rest: eighty and then four are added one at a time

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, add the parts. Ten thousand and one thousand two hundred make eleven thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Add eighty to get eleven thousand two hundred and eighty. Add four to get eleven thousand two hundred and eighty four.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: compare: Everest is 8848 m, which is less than 11284 m

marks.cmp: the doubled bar of 11284 is placed beside the bar of Everest of 8848
marks.low: the bar of Everest falls short of the doubled bar

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>Step four, compare the doubled height with Everest.
<bookmark mark='low'/>Everest is eight thousand eight hundred and forty eight metres. That is less than the doubled height.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 11284 m, which is more than 8848 m, so Everest is not twice as tall as Elbrus

marks.ans: the doubled height is boxed beside the bar of Everest

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Everest is not twice as tall as Elbrus, because twice Elbrus is more than Everest.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says Everest really is twice as tall; the doubled bar of Elbrus rises above the bar of Everest; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.over: the doubled bar of Elbrus rises above the bar of Everest

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks Everest really is twice as tall as Elbrus, because the picture shows it.
<bookmark mark='over'/>But the doubled bar of Elbrus rises above Everest.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The numbers decide, and a picture can mislead us.
